text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Finance minister Mogens Lykketoft is to present the Conservatives with 1997 budget plans to cut the household owner-occupier levy and raise the overall tax burden.

--- With the help of a foreign debt-collecting agency Danish tax authorities are now initiating a search for 3,000 Danes and foreigners who have left the country without paying back a total amount of 330 million crowns in study loans.

--- Maersk Oil, owned by shipping group A.P. Moeller, is part of an international consortium, formed by oil companies British Lasmo and US Anadarko Algeria Corporation, which has now found a large oil and gas field in Algeria estimated at 1.5 billion barrels of oil and gas at least.
--- Health minister Yvonne Herloev Andersen is now looking into the possibility of financing permanent treatment of pathological gamblers with profits from national footballs pools and lottery money.
--- A number of Danish hospitals have ended employment of foreign doctors as different qualifications and lack of Danish language skills have lowered treatment standards.

--- Half of all PC programmes used by Danish companies are pirated editions, meaning that software producers lost 500 million crowns turnover last year, a new report from two large software producers' associations shows.
--- Tele Danmark Mobil, part of telecom group Tele Danmark, is to lower basic prices on all NMT 900 system mobile calls from 2.35 crown to 1.95 per minute.
